title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 23 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Chronicles chapter 23 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 23 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Chronicles Chapter 23.

questions.question: In 2 Chronicles 23, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Jehoiada took captains of hundreds into covenant
The Levites gathered from all cities of Judah
All the congregation made a covenant with the king
A third part of priests and Levites shall be porters of the doors
questions.correctAnswer: Jehoiada took captains of hundreds into covenant
questions.explanation: The first event mentioned in the chapter is Jehoiada strengthening himself and taking captains of hundreds into covenant, as stated in 2 Chronicles 23:1.

questions.question: Who did Jehoiada take into covenant with him according to 2 Chronicles 23?
options: Azariah the son of Jeroham, Ishmael the son of Jehohanan, Azariah the son of Obed, Maaseiah the son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat the son of Zichri
The priests and Levites of Jerusalem
The elders of Judah and Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Azariah the son of Jeroham, Ishmael the son of Jehohanan, Azariah the son of Obed, Maaseiah the son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat the son of Zichri
questions.explanation: Jehoiada took these specific captains of hundreds into covenant with him, as listed in 2 Chronicles 23:1.

questions.question: From where did they gather the Levites according to 2 Chronicles 23?
options: Out of all the cities of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: Out of all the cities of Judah
questions.explanation: They gathered the Levites from all the cities of Judah, as stated in 2 Chronicles 23:2.

questions.question: Where did all the congregation make a covenant with the king?
questions.correctAnswer: In the house of God
questions.explanation: All the congregation made a covenant with the king in the house of God, as said in 2 Chronicles 23:3.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 23, who shall reign?
options: The chief of the fathers of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The king's son
questions.explanation: The king's son shall reign, as the LORD hath said of the sons of David, according to 2 Chronicles 23:3.

questions.question: What fraction of the priests and Levites shall be porters of the doors on the Sabbath?
questions.correctAnswer: A third part
questions.explanation: A third part of the priests and Levites shall be porters of the doors on the Sabbath, as described in 2 Chronicles 23:4.

questions.question: Where shall the second third part of the priests and Levites be stationed?
options: At the gate of the foundation
In the courts of the house of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: At the king's house
questions.explanation: A third part shall be at the king's house, as stated in 2 Chronicles 23:5.

questions.question: Where shall the final third part of the priests and Levites be stationed according to 2 Chronicles 23?
options: At the gate of the foundation
questions.correctAnswer: At the gate of the foundation
questions.explanation: The last third part shall be at the gate of the foundation, as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 23:5.

questions.question: Who is allowed to enter the house of the LORD according to 2 Chronicles 23?
options: Only the priests and those who minister of the Levites
questions.correctAnswer: Only the priests and those who minister of the Levites
questions.explanation: Only the priests and those who minister of the Levites shall go into the house of the LORD because they are holy, as stated in 2 Chronicles 23:6.

questions.question: Where shall all the people keep the watch of the LORD?
options: In the courts of the house of the LORD
At the gate of the foundation
questions.correctAnswer: In the courts of the house of the LORD
questions.explanation: All the people shall keep the watch of the LORD in the courts of the house of the LORD, as implied in 2 Chronicles 23:5-6.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 23, what shall the Levites do around the king?
options: Compass the king round about, every man with his weapons in his hand
Stand at the gates of the city
Serve as porters at the doors
questions.correctAnswer: Compass the king round about, every man with his weapons in his hand
questions.explanation: The Levites shall compass the king round about with weapons in hand, as stated in 2 Chronicles 23:7.

questions.question: True or False: In 2 Chronicles 23, the king's son is declared to reign as the LORD has said.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 23:3 states that the king's son shall reign, as the LORD hath said of the sons of David.

questions.question: True or False: The Levites are given the responsibility to guard the king when he comes in and goes out.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 23:7 says the Levites shall be with the king when he cometh in and when he goeth out.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Chronicles 23 says that all the people shall enter into the house of the LORD freely.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 23:6 states that none shall come into the house of the LORD except the priests and those who minister of the Levites, so this statement is false.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Chronicles 23, a third part of the priests and Levites shall serve as porters of the doors on the Sabbath.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 23:4 clearly states that a third part of the priests and Levites shall be porters of the doors on the Sabbath.

medium.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 23 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Chronicles Chapter 23 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Jehoiada the priest deliver to the captains of hundreds?
questions.correctAnswer: Spears, bucklers, and shields
questions.explanation: Jehoiada the priest delivered to the captains of hundreds spears, and bucklers, and shields, that had been king David's, which were in the house of God. (2 Chronicles 23:9)

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 23:10 promise will happen if someone follows Jehoiada's command about the people?
options: They will be equipped for battle
questions.correctAnswer: They will be equipped for battle
questions.explanation: Jehoiada commanded that every man should have his weapon in his hand, indicating that those who follow his command will be prepared for battle. (2 Chronicles 23:10)

questions.question: What did the people do when the king's son was brought out?
questions.correctAnswer: They praised him
questions.explanation: The people rejoiced and sounded with trumpets, praising the king when he was brought out. (2 Chronicles 23:13)

questions.question: What is the significance of Athaliah's reaction when she heard praise for the king?
questions.correctAnswer: She accused them of treason
questions.explanation: Athaliah rent her clothes and accused the people of treason upon hearing the noise of their praise. (2 Chronicles 23:13)

questions.question: What role did the Levites have according to Jehoiada's instructions?
options: They were to guard the temple
They were to lead the army
They were to teach the people
questions.correctAnswer: They were to guard the temple
questions.explanation: Jehoiada instructed the Levites to compass the king round about, indicating their protective role. (2 Chronicles 23:7)

questions.question: How did Jehoiada organize the people for the king's protection?
questions.correctAnswer: In sections around the temple
questions.explanation: Jehoiada set the people, every man having his weapon, from the right side of the temple to the left side, indicating a strategic organization. (2 Chronicles 23:10)

questions.question: What was the response of Jehoiada to Athaliah's presence?
questions.correctAnswer: He ordered her execution
questions.explanation: Jehoiada commanded that Athaliah be taken out and said that whoever follows her should be slain. (2 Chronicles 23:14)

questions.question: What does the crowning of the king's son symbolize in terms of God's promise?
questions.correctAnswer: The fulfillment of God's covenant
questions.explanation: The crowning of the king's son was a direct fulfillment of God's promise regarding the lineage of David. (2 Chronicles 23:3)

questions.question: What was the reaction of the people when the king stood at his pillar?
questions.correctAnswer: They rejoiced and sounded trumpets
questions.explanation: The people of the land rejoiced and sounded with trumpets at the sight of the king. (2 Chronicles 23:13)

questions.question: What did Jehoiada ensure regarding the Levites during the ceremony?
options: They were to lead the worship
They were to be armed and ready
They were to leave the temple
questions.correctAnswer: They were to be armed and ready
questions.explanation: Jehoiada instructed the Levites to be with the king and have their weapons in hand, ensuring they were ready for protection. (2 Chronicles 23:7)

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 23:1 indicate about Jehoiada's actions?
questions.correctAnswer: He took decisive action
questions.explanation: In the seventh year, Jehoiada strengthened himself and took the captains into covenant, showing his decisive leadership. (2 Chronicles 23:1)

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 23:6 say about who can enter the house of the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Only the priests and Levites
questions.explanation: The verse states that only the priests and those who minister of the Levites are allowed to enter the house of the LORD. (2 Chronicles 23:6)

questions.question: Is it true that the people of Judah responded positively to the anointing of the king?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The people rejoiced and praised the king when he was anointed, which indicates a positive response. (2 Chronicles 23:11)

questions.question: Is it false that Athaliah supported the anointing of the king?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Athaliah rejected the anointing and accused the people of treason, demonstrating her opposition. (2 Chronicles 23:13)

questions.question: Is it false that Jehoiada dismissed the courses of the priests and Levites?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jehoiada did not dismiss the courses, as the Levites and all Judah followed his commands diligently. (2 Chronicles 23:8)

hard.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 23 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Chronicles Chapter 23.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 23:15, where was Athaliah slain after being brought out?
options: At the entering of the horse gate by the king's house
In the house of the LORD
At the gate of the foundation
questions.correctAnswer: At the entering of the horse gate by the king's house
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 23:15 explicitly states that Athaliah was slain at the entering of the horse gate by the king's house after they laid hands on her.

questions.question: What covenant did Jehoiada make according to 2 Chronicles 23:16?
options: That they should be the LORD'S people
That they would rebuild the temple
That they would war against the Philistines
questions.correctAnswer: That they should be the LORD'S people
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 23:16 states Jehoiada made a covenant between himself, the people, and the king that they should be the LORD'S people.

questions.question: What did the people do to the house of Baal as described in 2 Chronicles 23:17?
options: They broke it down, broke its altars and images, and slew Mattan the priest
They rebuilt it with great honor
They made it a sanctuary for the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: They broke it down, broke its altars and images, and slew Mattan the priest
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 23:17 describes how the people destroyed the house of Baal, broke the altars and images, and put Mattan the priest to death before the altars.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 23:18, how did Jehoiada organize the service in the house of the LORD?
options: By appointing priests and Levites to offer burnt offerings with rejoicing and singing
By ordering a fast and silence
By sending the people to worship Baal
By building a new altar for sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: By appointing priests and Levites to offer burnt offerings with rejoicing and singing
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 23:18 explains that Jehoiada appointed offices for priests and Levites to offer burnt offerings with rejoicing and singing as ordained by David and written in the law of Moses.

questions.question: What role did Jehoiada assign to porters at the gates of the house of the LORD according to 2 Chronicles 23:19?
options: To prevent those who were unclean from entering
To welcome all people to enter
To sell offerings to the people
questions.correctAnswer: To prevent those who were unclean from entering
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 23:19 states Jehoiada set the porters at the gates to ensure that none who were unclean in any way would enter the house of the LORD.

questions.question: What was the reaction of the people after Jehoiada brought down the king and set him on the throne according to 2 Chronicles 23:21?
options: The people rejoiced and the city was quiet
The people rebelled against the king
The city was filled with mourning
The people fled into the wilderness
questions.correctAnswer: The people rejoiced and the city was quiet
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 23:21 describes that all the people rejoiced and the city was quiet after they had slain Athaliah and set the king on the throne.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'chathaph' (חָתַף) in 2 Chronicles 23:15 mean?
options: To seize or lay hands upon
questions.correctAnswer: To seize or lay hands upon
questions.explanation: In 2 Chronicles 23:15, the Hebrew word 'chathaph' means 'to seize or lay hands upon,' describing how they laid hands on Athaliah before taking her out to be slain.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in 2 Chronicles 23:20 when describing the bringing down of the king and setting him on the throne?
options: Inclusio, framing the narrative with the king's presence
Parallelism, contrasting the king and the people
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio, framing the narrative with the king's presence
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 23:20 uses inclusio by framing the narrative around the king's movement and enthronement, which brackets the restoration of David's line, a common literary device in Chronicles.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects to the theme of covenant renewal and kingship found in 2 Chronicles 23:16?
questions.correctAnswer: Joshua 24:25-27
questions.explanation: Joshua 24:25-27 recounts a covenant renewal between Joshua, the people, and the LORD, paralleling the covenant made by Jehoiada, the people, and the king in 2 Chronicles 23:16.

questions.question: Which New Testament event echoes the overthrow of Athaliah and establishment of rightful kingship in 2 Chronicles 23:21?
options: The anointing of Jesus as King in Luke 1:32
The Sermon on the Mount in Matthew 5
The Conversion of Saul in Acts 9
questions.correctAnswer: The anointing of Jesus as King in Luke 1:32
questions.explanation: Luke 1:32 speaks of Jesus being anointed as King over Israel, fulfilling the Davidic kingship theme restored in 2 Chronicles 23:21 after Athaliah's overthrow.

questions.question: What immediately precedes the execution of Athaliah in 2 Chronicles 23:15?
options: Jehoiada commands the captains to bring her out and not slay her in the house of the LORD
The people break down the house of Baal
The priests sing praises and play instruments
questions.correctAnswer: Jehoiada commands the captains to bring her out and not slay her in the house of the LORD
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 23:14 immediately precedes 23:15 and records Jehoiada instructing the captains to bring Athaliah out of the ranges and not to slay her in the house of the LORD.

questions.question: What is the significance of Jehoiada distributing the offices of the house of the LORD by the hand of the priests and Levites as described in 2 Chronicles 23:18?
options: It restores proper Levitical worship as ordained by David and the law of Moses
It establishes a new religious system
It grants political power to the Levites
It introduces Baal worship into the temple
questions.correctAnswer: It restores proper Levitical worship as ordained by David and the law of Moses
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 23:18 emphasizes that Jehoiada's appointments restored the Levitical offices to offer burnt offerings with rejoicing and singing, conforming to David's ordinance and Mosaic law.

questions.question: How does the role of the Levites in 2 Chronicles 23:7 demonstrate a typology of protection for the Davidic king?
options: Levites encircle the king with weapons, symbolizing divine protection over the monarchy
Levites lead the people in sacrifices
Levites serve as scribes and historians
Levites act as mediators between Baal and the king
questions.correctAnswer: Levites encircle the king with weapons, symbolizing divine protection over the monarchy
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 23:7 shows Levites surrounding the king with weapons, typologically representing God's protection of the Davidic line during political turmoil.

questions.question: Which literary device is used in 2 Chronicles 23:13 when Athaliah cries 'Treason, Treason'?
questions.correctAnswer: Repetition for emphasis
questions.explanation: In 2 Chronicles 23:13, Athaliah repeats the word 'Treason' to emphasize her alarm and accusation, a clear use of repetition as a literary device.

questions.question: The Levites acted as a military guard around the king in 2 Chronicles 23:7.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 23:7 states that the Levites compassed the king round about, every man with his weapons in his hand, acting as his guard.

theological.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 23 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Chronicles Chapter 23 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 23:3 teach about God's providential covenant with David's lineage?
options: God sovereignly establishes the Davidic covenant ensuring his son's reign
God permits human kingship without divine involvement
The monarchy is based solely on human political power
God rejects dynastic promises in favor of tribal leadership
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly establishes the Davidic covenant ensuring his son's reign
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 23:3 states, 'Behold, the king's son shall reign, as the LORD hath said of the sons of David,' demonstrating God's sovereign covenant promise concerning David's lineage.

questions.question: What doctrine about sanctification and separation is taught in 2 Chronicles 23:6?
options: Only the priests and Levites, being holy, may enter the house of the LORD
All people may enter the house of the LORD without distinction
Sanctification involves social status rather than holiness
The temple is accessible to everyone regardless of ritual purity
questions.correctAnswer: Only the priests and Levites, being holy, may enter the house of the LORD
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 23:6 declares that only priests and ministering Levites may enter the house of the LORD because 'they are holy,' teaching the doctrine of sanctification and sacred separation.

questions.question: What doctrine about covenant community and leadership is revealed in 2 Chronicles 23:16?
options: The king, priest, and people form a covenant people dedicated to the LORD
The king rules independently of the people's covenant with God
Covenantal relationship is only between individuals and God, ignoring leadership
The people reject covenant with the king in favor of tribal autonomy
questions.correctAnswer: The king, priest, and people form a covenant people dedicated to the LORD
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 23:16 states that Jehoiada made a covenant between himself, the people, and the king that they should be the LORD'S people, illustrating the doctrine of covenant community under God’s rule.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 23:4 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Divine order and sovereignty
questions.explanation: In 2 Chronicles 23:4, Jehoiada organizes the priests and Levites by a third part system, reflecting God’s attribute of sovereign order in the administration of His house.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is particularly highlighted in 2 Chronicles 23:11 during the anointing of the king?
questions.correctAnswer: Covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 23:11 shows the anointing of the king as fulfillment of God's promise to David, demonstrating God’s covenant faithfulness in upholding His word.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 23:17 connect to the broader biblical theme of true worship versus idolatry?
options: It shows the eradication of Baal worship prefiguring the prophetic call to exclusive worship of Yahweh
It endorses syncretism between Baal and Yahweh worship
It ignores the problem of idolatry in Israel
It presents Baal worship as acceptable alongside the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the eradication of Baal worship prefiguring the prophetic call to exclusive worship of Yahweh
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 23:17 recounts the destruction of Baal's temple and altar, reinforcing the biblical theme that true worship is exclusive to Yahweh, as emphasized by the prophets.

questions.question: In what way does the coronation of the king in 2 Chronicles 23:20 prefigure Christ's kingship in the New Testament?
options: It anticipates the Messiah as the rightful and anointed King on the throne of David
It denies the future Messianic hope
It presents kings as purely political figures with no spiritual significance
It portrays kingship as temporary and unrelated to divine promises
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates the Messiah as the rightful and anointed King on the throne of David
questions.explanation: The installation of the king on David's throne in 2 Chronicles 23:20 prefigures Christ’s eternal kingship as the Messiah, fulfilling God’s covenant promises to David.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Chronicles 23:9 and 2 Chronicles 23:10 teach about divine protection and leadership?
options: God equips His leaders and people with the means (weapons) for protection and order in His service
Divine protection is irrelevant to earthly leadership
Weapons symbolize human pride apart from God
God forbids any preparation for defense
questions.correctAnswer: God equips His leaders and people with the means (weapons) for protection and order in His service
questions.explanation: Verses 9 and 10 describe Jehoiada providing king David's weapons to captains and positioning armed men around the temple, teaching that God sustains leadership and His people through provision and order.

questions.question: What doctrine about covenant renewal and worship order is taught by the combination of 2 Chronicles 23:18 and 2 Chronicles 23:19?
options: Proper worship requires appointed priests and Levites maintaining holiness and order in the temple
Worship is spontaneous and without structure
Anyone may perform sacrifices regardless of priestly appointment
Ritual purity is unnecessary for worship
questions.correctAnswer: Proper worship requires appointed priests and Levites maintaining holiness and order in the temple
questions.explanation: Verses 18 and 19 emphasize the ordination of Levites for offerings and the guarding of temple gates to exclude the unclean, teaching the doctrine of orderly, holy worship under God’s covenant.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Chronicles 23:1 and 2 Chronicles 23:2 teach about leadership and communal covenant participation?
options: Leadership must unite the people in covenant and gather the faithful for communal commitment to God
Leadership is isolated from the people and acts independently
Communal covenant is a private matter with no public expression
Faithful leadership disregards the need for covenant renewal
questions.correctAnswer: Leadership must unite the people in covenant and gather the faithful for communal commitment to God
questions.explanation: Verse 1 shows Jehoiada taking captains into covenant, and verse 2 describes gathering Levites and chiefs, indicating that godly leadership fosters communal covenant renewal.

questions.question: Skeptics claim that 2 Chronicles 23:14-15 endorses unlawful violence by ordering Athaliah's death. What does the passage actually teach?
options: It teaches lawful execution outside the sanctuary, respecting the holiness of God's house
It endorses indiscriminate violence without limits
It promotes killing within the temple grounds
It shows that priests have no regard for human life
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches lawful execution outside the sanctuary, respecting the holiness of God's house
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 23:14 instructs not to kill Athaliah inside the LORD's house and 23:15 shows she was slain outside the sanctuary, demonstrating respect for temple holiness and lawful capital punishment.

questions.question: What doctrine about the nature of God's kingdom is presented in 2 Chronicles 23:21?
options: God’s kingdom brings peace and order after judgment upon evil
God’s kingdom is characterized by chaos and unrest
questions.correctAnswer: God’s kingdom brings peace and order after judgment upon evil
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 23:21 states that after Athaliah was slain, the city was quiet and the people rejoiced, illustrating that God's righteous judgment ushers in peace in His kingdom.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is emphasized in 2 Chronicles 23:12 when Athaliah hears the noise and comes into the house of the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s providential control over events
questions.explanation: Athaliah’s coming in response to the noise in 2 Chronicles 23:12 highlights God's providential orchestration of events to fulfill His plans.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 23:7 illustrate the theological principle of divine protection and holiness in leadership?
options: The Levites protect the king with weapons, signifying the holiness and security surrounding God’s anointed leader
The king is left undefended and vulnerable
The Levites act independently without concern for the king
questions.correctAnswer: The Levites protect the king with weapons, signifying the holiness and security surrounding God’s anointed leader
questions.explanation: Verse 7 shows Levites with weapons guarding the king, teaching that divine holiness requires protection of God's chosen ruler.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about ritual purity and worship does 2 Chronicles 23:5 and 2 Chronicles 23:19 teach?
options: Worship requires proper order and exclusion of the unclean to maintain holiness
Ritual purity is irrelevant to worship
Everyone may enter the temple without restriction
The temple is a place of social gathering only
questions.correctAnswer: Worship requires proper order and exclusion of the unclean to maintain holiness
questions.explanation: Verse 5 organizes people in the temple courts, and verse 19 sets porters to prevent the unclean from entering, together teaching that worship demands holiness and order.
